text:
I need to tell our staff that we're ending fully remote work. I'm one of the three partners at an architecture firm with 46 architects and designers.

What I can say:
- From September 1, everyone works in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
- 15 of our people were hired as fully remote in 2021 and 2022. 4 of them live more than two hours from the office.
- Those 4 can keep working remotely until the end of next year. After that, they come in once a week.
- Last year we lost two large hospital projects in the final interview. Both clients told us our team seemed not to know each other.
- Based on our review records, junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project.
- The partners have been coming in one day a week. We'll be in all three days too.

Keep it to one page. It goes out by email before an all-staff meeting on Friday.

Before I draft this, I have five questions. The answers will change what the email says.

1. **Dates.** Today is 16 November 2026, so I'm reading "September 1" as 1 September 2027. Does "until the end of next year" mean 31 December 2027, or the end of 2028? If it's December 2027, the four long-distance staff get only four months longer than everyone else. I'd write that differently from a full extra year.

2. **The other 11 remote hires.** They're within two hours of the office but were hired as fully remote. Is the firm offering them anything, such as help with travel costs, more time to adjust, or a way to ask for an exception for caregiving or health reasons? If not, should the email say so plainly?

3. **Talking to people first.** Will the 15 remote hires, especially the 4, hear about this from a partner before the email goes out? If they will, the email can mention it. If they won't, it's worth considering, because they're the people most likely to feel a promise has been broken.

4. **Mondays and Fridays.** Are those still open for remote work, or up to each person? Is there anything else people will want to know, like desks, parking, or core hours?

5. **Sign-off.** Should it come from all three partners by name, or from you?

If you don't know the answer to any of these, say so and I'll write the email without that part.

1. End of next year means 31 December 2027.

2. Anyone who lives more than 30 miles away gets up to $150 a month toward commuting. That's it. I can't offer exceptions to anyone beyond the 4, so yes, say that plainly.

3. I don't know.

4. I don't know about Mondays and Fridays. On desks: we don't have one for everyone yet, and new desks arrive in August. Other things: 5 of our 6 project leads already come in three days a week on their own. We'll review the policy with staff after six months. The all-staff meeting is Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio, and questions before then can go to me or HR.

5. From me, Paul Whitaker.

I've written the email from Paul. It's about 430 words, so it fits on one page.

<final_document>
**Subject: Three office days a week from 1 September 2027**

Everyone,

From 1 September 2027, everyone at the firm will work in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. This ends fully remote work at the firm. I want to explain why we're doing it, what it means for the people most affected, and what we can and can't offer.

For 15 of you, this changes what you were told when you joined. You were hired as fully remote in 2021 and 2022, and many of you have organised your lives around that. We are going back on that arrangement, and I won't pretend it's a small thing.

**Why we're doing this**

Last year we lost two large hospital projects at the final interview. Both clients told us the same thing: our team seemed not to know each other. That cost us work we wanted and were capable of doing.

We're seeing the same problem inside the firm. Our review records show that junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project. People learn much of what it takes to lead by working next to people who already do it. We haven't been giving our newer colleagues enough of that.

**What this asks of the partners**

The three partners have been coming in one day a week. From September, we'll be in all three days as well. Five of our six project leads already come in three days a week on their own.

**If you live a long way from the office**

Four of you live more than two hours from the office. You can keep working remotely until 31 December 2027. From January 2028, we're asking you to come in one day a week. I know that gives you only four months longer than everyone else.

Anyone who lives more than 30 miles from the office can claim up to $150 a month toward commuting costs.

Apart from those four colleagues, we can't make individual exceptions. I'd rather tell you that now than leave you hoping for one.

**Practical points**

- **Desks:** We don't have a desk for everyone yet. New desks arrive in August, before the change begins.
- **Review:** Six months after the change starts, we'll review the policy with staff.

**Friday**

We'll go through all of this at the all-staff meeting on Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio. If you have questions before then, or something you'd rather raise privately, please come to me or to HR.

Paul Whitaker
Partner
</final_document>

- **Mondays and Fridays:** The email doesn't mention them because you weren't sure of the rule. Expect someone to ask on Friday, so it's worth having an answer ready.
- **Telling people first:** If you can, have a partner tell the four long-distance staff, and ideally all 15 remote hires, before the email goes out. This is the group most likely to feel let down, and hearing it from a partner first will make a difference.
- **Desks:** The email says only that the new desks arrive in August. Check that this covers everyone before anyone takes it as a promise of a desk each.
- **Review timing:** I took "after six months" to mean six months after 1 September 2027, so around March 2028.
